name: Nogent-le-Roi
summary: A town where Philip VI of France died in 1350.
overview: Nogent-le-Roi was a town in northern France associated with the death of Philip VI, the first Valois king.
His death in 1350 came after the opening disasters of the Hundred Years’ War and the arrival of plague.

contentSections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Nogent-le-Roi in the Eure-et-Loir was a royal estate and small town in the contested landscape between the Capetian royal domain and Normandy. Philip VI of France died there in 1350.

contentSections.title: Legacy
paragraphs: Philip VI's death at Nogent-le-Roi closed the first Valois reign — a period defined by the disputed succession that started the Hundred Years' War, the English victories at Crécy and Calais, and the arrival of the Black Death in 1348. He left John II a kingdom strained by military defeat, financial pressure, and demographic catastrophe.
